A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectral diffusion and schedule-design work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including appendices A–M in v1 and A–N in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian simulations, dataset-derived schedule optimization, and MUSIC generation experiments evaluated with Wasserstein-2 distance and Frobenius norm.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds CIFAR-10 generation results, empirical SC09 evaluation, temporal-dynamics analyses and optimization-time measurements.

M1.justification: Schedule construction is generalized from circulant covariance approximation and Fourier analysis to general covariance eigendecomposition (Sections 3.3–4). The circulant-fitting procedure required in v1 and derived in its Appendix M is removed. This broadens the method's admissible covariance structure while retaining the SLSQP optimization framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 image experiments under both fitted-Gaussian and neural-denoiser settings. It also extends SC09 from Gaussian-derived scheduling experiments to generation with a trained neural denoiser (Appendix J). Synthetic Gaussian and MUSIC coverage remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding MUSIC comparison retains Linear, EDM, three Cosine variants and three Sigmoid variants. The isotropic-Gaussian AYS comparison is retained in Appendix G.2 rather than newly introduced. Added benchmark comparisons use the existing heuristic schedule families.

E3.justification: V2 introduces CIFAR-10 FID evaluation with a pretrained continuous-noise denoiser and removes MUSIC Frobenius-norm evaluation. The reported MUSIC synthesis budget changes from 1,000 samples to 20,000 in Appendix J, although Section 6.3 says 50,000. These establish substantial protocol revisions, with the exact audio sample count unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix K.2 adds analyses of eigenvalue evolution, relative-error trajectories and Wasserstein-2 error throughout sampling (Figures 23–25), extending v1's final-output analyses. Appendix N adds optimization-time scaling across step counts and covariance dimensions. Earlier initialization, mean-bias and DDPM-versus-DDIM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 first reports three independent CIFAR-10 runs and mean scores with 95% confidence intervals calculated using standard errors and the t-distribution (Appendix J, Tables 1–2). V1 provides no corresponding uncertainty estimates. The listed seed ranges contain 5,000 seeds each despite the stated 50,000 samples per run, leaving their mapping unclear.

E6.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 FID/Wasserstein results, Gaussian-audio Wasserstein comparisons, empirical SC09 results and runtime measurements. Table 2 reports spectral FID 12.50 at 10 steps; at 90 steps, EDM scores 2.52 versus spectral's 2.60. These are newly reported results, not cross-version performance gains. V1's MUSIC Frobenius results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 removes the circulant/shift-invariance restriction, adds joint-diagonalization Lemma 3.3, and revises the DDIM/DDPM derivations for general covariance eigenbases. V1's circulant-approximation derivation disappears. Separately, v2's main KL equation (16) introduces sign errors relative to v1 equation (17), while Appendix D equation (38) retains the correct expression.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and closing discussion broaden the analysis from Gaussianity plus shift invariance to Gaussianity alone. V2 also explicitly identifies analysis of evolving spectral properties throughout sampling as a core contribution, extending the earlier emphasis on the output transfer function and schedule design.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of temporal error behavior and distinguishes eigenvalue convergence speed from final accuracy (Appendix K.2). It discusses approximation error from discrete schedule matching, limitations of FAD for the audio settings, and optimization costs at high resolution, with PCA or low-rank approximation suggested as mitigation.

D1.justification: New documentation includes MUSIC batch size 64, nearest-training-step schedule matching, the SC09 architecture source, and explicit CIFAR-10 schedules for 10, 20 and 28 steps. Appendix N supplies optimizer iteration limits, tolerance and CPU execution information. These are largely new disclosures rather than evidence that previously unspecified implementation settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Wang and Vastola's Gaussian-score analysis, Crabbé et al.'s frequency-domain diffusion work, CIFAR-10 and FAD. Related work more explicitly contrasts continuous Gaussian solutions with the paper's discrete analysis. The central positioning around data-dependent spectral schedule design remains.

P1.justification: The title changes, substantial portions of the abstract, introduction and related work are rewritten, and terminology shifts toward general spectral coordinates. Experimental subsections and discussion are reorganized, and the appendix structure is substantially revised beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. V1 Figures 1–3 are combined into v2 Figure 1, AYS and DDPM comparisons move to appendices, and empirical displays are reorganized around multiple datasets. V2 adds temporal-dynamics figures and three tables, while removing the MUSIC covariance display and Frobenius plot.

improvement.justification: General covariance analysis and new CIFAR-10 FID and neural SC09 experiments substantially address v1's restrictive assumptions and narrow real-data validation. Explicit schedules, uncertainty estimates and runtime limitations improve assessability. These gains outweigh the new main-text KL sign inconsistency, whose correct derivation remains in Appendix D, and the unresolved sample-count and seed descriptions; those issues still need correction.
